ring: Fenrir — the wolf and the moon
summary: Revise, 7.0. This is revival round 1; earlier scores were 5.5, 6.5 and 7.0 (cut). Caiman is 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. The head moved in the right direction. The muzzle is 6.66 mm stop to nose, up from 5.5. The lower-jaw-to-muzzle ratio is 1.08, down from 1.45. The chin reaches 7.22 mm. The lower jaw is now tied to the cheeks by a continuous run of metal down each side. The upper flew is broken at the canines instead of running as one horseshoe. The fangs read as four curved canines, and the moonstone is held and visible. Shown without the caption, face-300 now reads as a wolf's head with an orb in its jaws more often than as a bulldog. It still does not clear 7.5. The head's surface is melted and blobby where it should be modelled. The broken flews read as segmented caterpillar rolls. The cheek fur is still worm-like squiggles. The nasal bridge is a flat plank with no nose leather at its end. The palm and shoulder relief, which is half the ring, has not moved. The Ruff is still combed vertical spikes and stacked chevrons with saw-toothed, stair-stepped outlines (close-ruff.png). The Gleipnir bindings are jagged ovals, not wraps (close-binding.png). A bare band still separates the head from the ruff, and seam_crease_run is 1.55 mm against the 0.7 mm asked for. Every gate in report.json is green. The template gate in verification.json, though, predates this round's design (it was written at 02:10, the design at 15:37, and its 1,257,542 triangles do not match the current 1,254,814), so it is not recorded for the ring as submitted. That alone forces revise. The head is close. The fur and bindings are the work.
strengths: A unique Bestiarium silhouette: a pricked-ear wolf mask on 010 stock with the moon in its jaws. Nothing else in the collection or in Reptilia looks like it (contact-300.png).

The jaw geometry was fixed as asked: muzzle 6.66 mm (was 5.5), lower jaw to muzzle 1.08 (was 1.45), chin reach 7.22 mm (was 8.0). The lower jaw now joins each cheek (face.png x 460-540 and 1060-1140).
The upper flew is notched at each canine sheath (close-head.png x 560-620 and 880-940), so the round-3 horseshoe specular is broken.
Four fang claws curve up the moonstone's dome with their tips on it (side.png, stones.png). The stone is the focal point and fully visible.
Ears are crisp, with an inner cup and strands (close-head.png). Brow, muzzle, eyes, chin and nose census show 0 creases of 60 deg or more.
The hollow under the head has a 1.11-1.46 mm roof and a 1.16-1.17 mm floor at theta 70/90/110 (section-*.png), at 31.7 g in 18k.
One theme face to palm: the wolf's head and moon, the fur ruff, and Gleipnir at the palm.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Head and moon on the face, ruff on the walls and shoulders, Gleipnir cord and bindings on the palm: one story. The bare band between head and ruff (hero.png x 880-910) weakens the hand-over but does not scatter it.

checklist.item: Reads as its creature at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: face-300.png: pointed ears, a long bridge, four fangs and a gaping jaw round an orb read as a wolf or fox head. It is marginal: the head is wide and round, so it can still read as a lynx or owl mask. hero-300.png reads as a beast's head biting a pearl.

close-ruff.png: every lock edge is saw-toothed and stair-stepped. close-binding.png: the binding wraps have jagged sawtooth rims and smeared diagonal streaks. On the head, the cheek fur is melted and smeared rather than drawn (close-head.png x 0-560 and 1040-1600, y 300-800).

checklist.item: Stones in made settings and visible
checklist.reason: A 10 mm moonstone cabochon held by four railless fang claws and the jaws. 1 reported, 1 previewed, no warnings. Fully visible face-on.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The head is sculpted, but its surface is lumpy and molten with no planes to hold light. The nasal bridge is a flat rectangular plank (close-head.png x 690-900, y 300-780). The flews are strings of sausage segments. The Ruff reads as mechanical stacked chevrons (reverse.png, shoulder.png).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The head and ruff cover the 010 face, and the band edges stay crisp (side.png, palm.png). Not much of the factory angle is left visible, but nothing was softened.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from Arachne, Manticora and the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: The eared mask standing over the orb is unique in the collection.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large (head, moon) and medium (ears, fangs, jaw) are there. The small scale is noise, not legible detail: combed spikes and smeared squiggles where Caiman's plates, pits and knobs each read cleanly (caiman/hero.png).

punch_list.zone: Layer 'Ruff' (0.6 mm), shoulders theta 20-70 and 110-160 and head walls: shoulder.png x 300-900, y 250-600; reverse.png x 420-1250, y 330-560; close-ruff.png
punch_list.change: Carried over from round 3 #4 and still open. Repaint the locks at 2-3x the atlas resolution, or as stamps, so their outlines are smooth. Widen the bases to 1.2-1.6 mm, cut the count about 30%, and sweep each S-bow 20-30 deg back along the band so the locks flow toward the palm instead of standing across it as vertical spikes. Drop the stacked-chevron rows.
punch_list.acceptance: close-ruff.png: no saw-tooth or stair-step on any lock rim. shoulder.png and reverse.png: no run of more than 4 parallel spikes, and each lock shows one pointed tip and a rounded crest. A 300 px shoulder crop reads as flowing fur. DFM stays at 0.

punch_list.change: Carried over from round 3 #7. Replace the molten squiggles with 2-3 tiers of pointed locks, 3-4 mm long, sweeping back toward the ears, each with a rounded crest, one centre groove and a clean edge. punch_list.acceptance: close-head.png: every cheek stroke is a lock with a pointed tip, with no closed worm shapes and no rippled specular between locks. The cheek census stays at 0 edges of 60 deg or more.
